description: Add LLM-based fact extraction to the memory system. Create src/nexus/memory/llm_extract.py with LLMFactExtractor that uses cheap LLM calls for structured fact extraction with cost guards, rate limiting, and fallback to existing regex-based extraction.
steps: Create src/nexus/memory/llm_extract.py with LLMFactExtractor class: (a) Constructor takes llm_callable (async function: prompt str -> response str), optional min_output_length (default 200 chars), optional max_calls_per_minute (default 10), optional prompt_template. (b) extract_facts() method: checks if output text length > min_output_length; if short, delegates to existing FactExtractor directly. (c) For longer outputs, calls LLM with structured prompt asking for JSON extraction of: decisions_made, tools_discovered, patterns_learned, errors_encountered. (d) Parses LLM JSON response into list[Fact] objects compatible with the existing Fact dataclass from nexus.memory.layered. (e) Falls back to FactExtractor.extract_facts() if LLM call fails or response is unparseable. (f) Rate limiting: tracks call timestamps, rejects if > max_calls_per_minute in rolling window (returns fallback extraction instead). (g) Docstring includes cost estimate: ~$0.001 per extraction call with GPT-4o-mini.

Create tests/test_llm_extract.py: (a) Test successful extraction with mocked LLM returning valid JSON with all 4 categories. (b) Test short text (< 200 chars) bypasses LLM and uses regex extraction directly. (c) Test fallback when LLM returns invalid JSON. (d) Test fallback when LLM callable raises exception. (e) Test rate limiting: make max_calls_per_minute=2, call 3 times rapidly, verify 3rd call uses fallback. (f) Test extracted facts have correct format (content, source_agent_id, metadata with fact_type). (g) Test configurable min_output_length threshold. (h) Test custom prompt template is used.
acceptance_criteria: LLMFactExtractor accepts async LLM callable as dependency
Short outputs (< min_output_length) bypass LLM and use regex extractor
Rate limiting prevents more than max_calls_per_minute LLM calls per rolling minute
Fallback to FactExtractor.extract_facts() works on LLM failure
Extracted facts are compatible with existing Fact dataclass
Existing tests still pass (no modifications to extract.py)
